notes: A flat oil day, a Trump deferral to the new year, an Israeli push for a short joint campaign, an IRGC rejection of the 'neither war nor peace' status quo, and no new confirmed hull hit. Oil: Thu 19 Nov Brent Jan-27 settled 91.98 (+0.03, +0.03%) after a ~$2 range (morning peak 93.50), Brent Feb-27 89.44 (+0.27) - the first in-gate M2 print in six runs, Jan/Feb backwardation 2.54; WTI Dec-26 83.21 (-0.05, -0.06%; expires Fri 20 Nov, lowest close since 26 Aug), WTI Jan-27 (more active) 82.44 (+0.13); Brent-WTI (Jan/Dec) 8.77. Brent down ~20% in November, on course for a third weekly loss (~-3.5%); Fri 20 Nov Asia Brent 92.22 at 01:18 GMT. Rabobank's Schmit: 'not yet at the point where the narrative of improving supply is enough to overshadow the military flare-ups'; Saxo's Hansen: 'liquidity is poor'; US energy chief says Hormuz flows reached a record, Rabobank says flows 'have improved' but ships still attacked; European diesel at a three-month low; OPEC+ ministerial 29 Nov. Plumbing: Trump to Axios from Air Force One (19 Nov, ~18:48 GMT): 'I am not rushing into any decision... We will see what happens after the beginning of the year'; NYT/Axios (early 19 Nov): Netanyahu pressing Washington for a four-to-seven-day joint air campaign (Pickaxe Mountain, bridges, power plants, leadership), US official: economic pressure 'devastating Iran', president 'does not have any need to conduct major combat operations', some in the administration see the Israeli chem/bio intelligence as 'driven by an agenda'; Channel 12 (ToI 20:59 local 19 Nov, censor-approved): Trump backed out of planned US strikes 'multiple times' in recent weeks, Israel readied each time, Netanyahu briefed by Gofman and Zamir with secrecy-guideline review 'resembling the lead-up to earlier attacks'; DTN: White House briefed on fresh attack options, third carrier (USS Theodore Roosevelt) in CENTCOM AOR while USS George Washington departs for Yokosuka. Iran side: IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi (19 Nov, to Basij students/IRNA): 'We will not accept the continuation of the current status quo, a state of neither war nor peace, or a war of attrition', 'We will bring the war to a definitive conclusion', 'either be settled on the battlefield, or the United States must accept Iran's conditions', Strait stays closed until US conditions met 'in a verifiable manner', 'We will not enter the nuclear issue until the matter of the Strait of Hormuz is resolved', 'We will not allow the continued naval, land, and air blockade'; Baghaei calls the chemical-weapons allegations 'fraudulent' (ToI 23:29). Mediators (Gulf News 20 Nov): Araghchi-Albusaidi talks on maritime security, no navigation agreement; Oman wants 'inclusion'; Qatar's Al Ansari calls the Hormuz closure an international crisis urging collective diplomacy - no venue, date or US participant. Washington: Senate rejects H.Con.Res.93 war-powers resolution 48-51 (Collins, Murkowski, Paul for; Fetterman against); Pentagon: war cost $48.3bn to 13 Nov; Duckworth joins Khanna/Ansari in conditioning funding. Maritime: no new UKMTO advisory in gate (212-26 remains the latest); JMIC warns further attacks on commercial vessels 'highly likely'; no new Iranian mine claim after the IRGC two-supertanker claim already recorded; Gulf News 20 Nov restates the three-tanker claim as unconfirmed; hormuz.now 19 Nov 21:50Z: 40 crossings/7d = 5.7/day (7%), 18 Nov finished at 9 (3 in / 6 out - the highest daily since early Nov), 19 Nov 3 so far; tankers 11/7d (1.6/day, ~3%), 390 tankers / 43 VLCC visible (up from 371); straits.live 19 Nov 05:30Z: 44 holding (43 on 18 Nov). Gulf front: Houthi debris damages the PIF tower in Riyadh (no injuries), Houthis claim King Khalid airport and the Financial Center; coalition intercepts a ballistic missile and two drones early Fri 20 Nov; Saudi reserves 'all necessary measures'. OFAC 19 Nov: counter-narcotics/cyber only, no Iran tag. Net: Strait closed, no deal, no new confirmed strike or hull hit, both capitals publicly rejecting the status quo while the market settles flat and the first Brent M2 print shows a $2.54 prompt backwardation.

items.name: ICE Brent January 2027 (M1) settle, Thu 19 Nov: 91.98 (+0.03, +0.03%)
items.source: DTN/Progressive Farmer 19 Nov 2:43pm CST (names January); Bloomberg via Rigzone 19 Nov 5:31pm EST ('January'); cappnotes Closing Look 19 Nov; Reuters via financefeeds 20 Nov
items.note: Four sources agree on 91.98; morning peak 93.50 (DTN), ~$2 range (Bloomberg), 'just below $92'. Brent down roughly 20% in November and on course for a third weekly loss (~-3.5% from 95.84 on 13 Nov). Drivers per DTN: Wednesday's EIA builds (crude +3.4 mb, gasoline +5.2 mb), trilateral pledge to boost refined-product supply, offset by reports the White House was briefed on fresh attack options, a third carrier group in region, the three-tanker mine report and Houthi launches at Riyadh. Rigzone/Bloomberg: Schmit (Rabobank) 'We are not yet at the point where the narrative of improving supply is enough to overshadow the military flare-ups'; Hansen (Saxo) 'Liquidity is poor across the markets'; US energy chief said Hormuz flows reached a record; Western officials say chance of another round of US mass strikes 'appeared to have grown'. Brent Jan - WTI Dec = 8.77 (vs 8.93 Wed).

items.name: ICE Brent February 2027 (M2) settle, Thu 19 Nov: 89.44 (+0.27, +0.30%); Jan/Feb prompt spread 2.54 backwardation
items.source: DTN/Progressive Farmer 19 Nov 2:43pm CST ('Brent February' line)
items.note: First dated M2 settle printed in six runs (last dated strip 15 Oct: Jan 103.17 / Feb 100.60, spread 2.57). Jan 91.98 - Feb 89.44 = 2.54 backwardation (computed, not printed by DTN), essentially unchanged from the 15 Oct 2.57 and consistent with Bloomberg's approximate ~2.80 relayed 17 Nov. M2 rose more than M1 (+0.27 vs +0.03), so the prompt spread narrowed ~24c on the day. Single source; Rigzone/Bloomberg, cappnotes and financefeeds print front month only. Note DTN says the Jan WTI contract is the 'more active' one, and the same will be true of Feb Brent after Jan Brent's 30 Nov expiry.

items.name: Trump to Axios from Air Force One (19 Nov, ~18:48 GMT): 'I am not rushing into any decision [on Iran]. We will see what happens after the beginning of the year' - no decision on next steps until 2027; US official (NYT/Axios): economic pressure is 'devastating Iran', the president 'does not have any need to conduct major combat operations' while keeping 'all options'
items.headline: Trump says he is 'not rushing into a decision' on Iran / Trump said weighing another Iran offensive as Netanyahu pushes 4- to 7-day campaign
items.claim: Middle East Eye liveblog (19 Nov 18:48 GMT): Trump told Axios (Barak Ravid) in a phone call from Air Force One returning from China, 'I am not rushing into any decision. We will see what happens after the beginning of the year'; MEE: he won't decide his next step in the Iran war until the new year. Times of Israel (19 Nov 02:18, citing NYT/Axios): Trump is reportedly weighing another major offensive but last week called it 'quite unlikely', reportedly heeding Gulf allies who favour maintaining economic pressure; a US official said economic pressure is 'devastating Iran' and the president 'does not have any need to conduct major combat operations' while 'all options' remain available; Axios: some in the administration see the Israeli chem/bio intelligence as 'driven by an agenda' tied to Netanyahu's post-election politics; NYT: the 'prevailing view' is Iran would not use such weapons pre-emptively. Rigzone/Bloomberg (19 Nov): Western officials said the chance of another round of US mass strikes 'appeared to have grown'. Gulf News 20 Nov: Iran called the chem/bio claims 'baseless'; Trump 'downplayed an imminent threat'.
items.source: Middle East Eye liveblog update 19 Nov 18:48 GMT; Times of Israel 19 Nov 02:18 (NYT/Axios relay); Rigzone/Bloomberg 19 Nov 5:31pm EST; Gulf News 20 Nov 09:06 UAE
items.note: Second explicit January-1 horizon in two days (Fox 'after January 1st' recorded 11-19), now framed as 'not rushing' rather than 'finish it off soon' - a softer edge than Wednesday's Fox interview but no mediator, venue, terms or Witkoff mention. Pairs with the Channel 12 'backed out multiple times' report (T4 hit) and the IRGC's rejection of 'neither war nor peace' (Iran-side T1 hit): both capitals are publicly describing the status quo, one as tolerable until 2027, the other as unacceptable. Scorer decides whether the deferral is a de-escalation tell or a hold.

items.name: Israel presses for a short joint campaign while Trump holds: NYT/Axios - Netanyahu pushing Washington to join a four-to-seven-day air campaign on Iran (targets could include Pickaxe Mountain underground site, bridges, power plants, military and civilian leadership); Channel 12 (censor-approved, 19 Nov evening) - Trump backed out of planned US strikes 'multiple times' in recent weeks, Israel readied each time, Netanyahu briefed by Gofman and Zamir with a secrecy-guidelines review 'resembling the lead-up to earlier attacks'; DTN: White House briefed on fresh attack options; USS Theodore Roosevelt in CENTCOM AOR as third carrier, USS George Washington departs after ~3 months
items.headline: Trump said weighing another Iran offensive as Netanyahu pushes 4- to 7-day campaign / Trump backed out of strikes on Iran multiple times in recent weeks - report / WTI Stuck Beneath $85 as Glut Fears Offset Supply Risks
items.claim: Times of Israel (19 Nov 02:18, citing NYT and Axios): Netanyahu is reportedly pushing Washington to join Israel in a limited four-to-seven-day campaign of airstrikes; per Axios targets could include Pickaxe Mountain, a suspected underground nuclear facility not yet struck, plus bridges, power plants, and military and civilian leadership; Mossad chief Gofman went to Washington last week with intelligence that Iran is advancing a chemical weapons programme; NYT: US intelligence has seen 'evidence of stepped-up efforts' by Iran on chemical and biological capacities, Israeli officials briefed the US on Iranian efforts to target US officials with such weapons; Pentagon and CIA declined comment. Times of Israel liveblog (19 Nov 8:59pm, ToI staff): Channel 12, in an unsourced report approved by the military censor, says Trump backed out of planned US strikes on Iran 'multiple times' in recent weeks - Israel prepared each time for an intended US attack but Trump 'changed his mind, and didn't give the order'; the censor blocked the count; an Israeli official: 'chances for offensive action against Iran are growing' but Israel awaits Trump's go-ahead; Channel 12 (two sources): Trump leaned more toward strikes after Gofman's visit; Netanyahu was briefed that night by Gofman, Zamir and other senior officials and participants were given a review of secrecy guidelines; US and Israeli officials are divided on whether Iran is succeeding in creating a chemical weapon; a source: 'if the US and Israel don't act now, they'll have to take military action at some later stage, but under harsher conditions'. DTN (19 Nov): 'Reports said the White House was briefed on fresh attack options against Iran. A third U.S. carrier strike group and thousands of amphibious forces arrived in the region.' Gulf News 20 Nov / ToI 09:07: USS Theodore Roosevelt arrived in the CENTCOM area (CENTCOM: scheduled deployment), USS George Washington left after about three months, reportedly for Yokosuka.
items.source: Times of Israel 19 Nov 02:18 (NYT/Axios relay) and liveblog entry 19 Nov 8:59pm (Channel 12); DTN 19 Nov 2:43pm CST; Gulf News 20 Nov 09:06 UAE; Times of Israel liveblog 19 Nov 05:37, 09:07
items.note: Strike-planning plumbing, not a strike: the new facts are (a) a concrete Israeli campaign proposal with a named target set and duration, (b) a censor-approved Israeli report that US strikes were ordered up and stood down more than once, and (c) a carrier rotation (three CSGs briefly, now GW leaving - net posture unchanged at two to three). Set against Trump's 'not rushing' and the US official's 'does not have any need', the balance reads as Israel pushing and Washington deferring to 2027. Haaretz's own 4-7 day report was robots_disallowed; ToI relay used. Mako joint-attack report and Cooper-Zamir-Gofman meeting recorded 11-19.

items.name: IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi (19 Nov, Tehran, to Basij students; IRNA/Xinhua): 'We will not accept the continuation of the current status quo, a state of neither war nor peace, or a war of attrition'; 'We will bring the war to a definitive conclusion'; 'This matter will either be settled on the battlefield, or the United States must accept Iran's conditions'; Strait 'will not be reopened unless the United States meets its conditions in a verifiable manner'; 'We will not enter the nuclear issue until the matter of the Strait of Hormuz is resolved'; 'We will not allow the continued naval, land, and air blockade'; Baghaei calls chemical-weapons allegations 'fraudulent'
items.headline: Iran's IRGC vows to challenge US blockade / Iran Not To Accept Continuation Of War Of Attrition: IRGC Spokesman / Iran Rules Out Nuclear Talks Until Strait of Hormuz Dispute Is Resolved / Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman calls chemical weapons allegations 'fraudulent'
items.claim: Middle East Eye (19 Nov 15:03 GMT): IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi, speaking to Basij students in Tehran: 'We will not allow the continued naval, land, and air blockade imposed on our country'; 'We will not accept the continuation of the current status quo, a state of neither war nor peace, or a war of attrition'; resolving the Strait of Hormuz issue is a precondition for discussing the nuclear programme. IANS via ommcomnews (20 Nov 01:54Z, citing Xinhua/IRNA): Iran 'does not accept the continuation of a war of attrition and will not let this situation persist for a long time'; 'We will bring the war to a definitive conclusion'; 'This matter will either be settled on the battlefield, or the United States must accept Iran's conditions'; Iran 'will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz unless the United States meets its conditions in a verifiable manner'; 'We will not enter the nuclear issue until the matter of the Strait of Hormuz is resolved'. Capital News Point (19 Nov 16:51Z): the Strait 'will not be reopened until seven conditions set by Iran are fulfilled' (conditions not listed), the US naval blockade must be lifted among them. Gulf News 20 Nov: Mohebbi rejected a continued war of attrition; Strait stays closed until US conditions met 'in a verifiable manner'. Rigzone/Bloomberg: per IRNA, Iran won't engage on nuclear weapons until the Hormuz question is settled. Times of Israel liveblog (19 Nov 11:29pm, headline only): Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei calls the chemical-weapons allegations 'fraudulent'; Gulf News: Iran called the claims 'baseless'.
items.source: Middle East Eye liveblog update 19 Nov 15:03 GMT; IANS/Xinhua/IRNA via ommcomnews 20 Nov 01:54Z; Capital News Point 19 Nov 16:51Z; Gulf News 20 Nov; Rigzone/Bloomberg 19 Nov; Times of Israel liveblog 19 Nov 11:29pm
items.note: Iran-side sequencing statement: Hormuz first, nuclear second, with 'verifiable' US compliance and a 'seven conditions' list (unpublished here) - the mirror of Trump's 'lasting deal'/'not rushing'. The 'definitive conclusion... battlefield or conditions' line is the most explicit IRGC rejection of the frozen status quo since the MOU collapse; it is rhetoric from a spokesman, not a Supreme National Security Council decision, and is paired with no new strike claim. Also readable as M1 (Iran's transit regime restated); labelled T1 for the deal-sequencing content. 'Seven conditions' text not surfaced - scorer may want it.

items.name: Mediator channel (Gulf News 20 Nov): Araghchi and Omani FM Badr Albusaidi held talks on maritime security, no final navigation agreement announced; Oman wants 'inclusion' in regional diplomacy; Qatar's Majed Al Ansari calls the Hormuz closure an international crisis and urges collective action and diplomacy - no US participant, venue or date; no Pakistan/Islamabad or Witkoff item
items.headline: US-Israel-Iran War: Key Updates for UAE Residents on Travel, Security, and Energy Disruptions (Nov 20)
items.claim: Gulf News (20 Nov, updated 09:06 UAE): Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari called the Hormuz closure an international crisis and urged collective action and diplomacy; Oman wants 'inclusion' in regional diplomacy; Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi and Omani FM Badr Albusaidi held talks on maritime security, but no final navigation agreement was announced. Capital News Point and MEE (19 Nov): no mediator named in the IRGC statements. Rigzone/Bloomberg (19 Nov): 'No specific negotiations are described' beyond diplomatic pressure on Trump.
items.source: Gulf News 20 Nov 09:06 UAE (single source; the Araghchi-Albusaidi item is undated within the brief and may restate the 17 Nov Muscat meeting recorded 11-17)
items.note: Weak T3: the only mediator items in gate are a Qatari call for diplomacy and an Omani request for 'inclusion'; the Araghchi-Albusaidi 'maritime security' talks may be the 17 Nov Muscat round (already recorded as 'no deal') restated by Gulf News - treat as not-new unless a dated second source appears. Third consecutive run with no Witkoff, Pakistan or Islamabad item and no dated US-Iran contact beyond Trump's 'we talked to them' (11-19).

items.name: Senate rejects H.Con.Res.93 war-powers resolution directing withdrawal from hostilities with Iran, 48-51 (Collins, Murkowski, Paul for; Fetterman against; Murphy absent) - first Iran vote since the GOP midterm losses; Pentagon deputy comptroller: war cost $48.3bn to 13 Nov (~26% above CBO's $38bn Aug estimate); Duckworth to oppose any funding bill that does not cut war funding (December shutdown risk)
items.headline: US Senate blocks Iran war powers resolution / Senate Rejects First Iran Resolution Since GOP's Midterm Losses
items.claim: Middle East Monitor/Anadolu (19 Nov 20:31Z): the Senate rejected H.Con.Res.93, sponsored by Rep. Seth Moulton and passed by the House 220-204 in September, by 48-51; Republicans Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Rand Paul voted in favour, Democrat John Fetterman against, Chris Murphy did not vote; the measure would direct Trump to withdraw US forces from hostilities with Iran. Gulf News (20 Nov): Pentagon deputy comptroller Arthur Miller said the war had cost more than $48.3bn as of 13 Nov, about 26% above the CBO's $38bn estimate as of 1 Aug, excluding base damage and global economic harm; Sen. Tammy Duckworth vowed to oppose any funding bill that doesn't cut war funding amid December shutdown concerns.
items.source: Middle East Monitor (Anadolu) 19 Nov 20:31Z; Gulf News 20 Nov 09:06 UAE; Bloomberg Government headline (not fetched)
items.note: Domestic constraint plumbing: the president retains war authority by three votes, with the funding fight (11 Dec deadline, Khanna/Ansari recorded 11-19, now Duckworth) the live lever. Not a deal or strike tell in itself; recorded because the Axios 'after the beginning of the year' timing and the December funding calendar now overlap. thehill.com client_error; Anadolu relay used.

items.name: Houthi-Saudi front: PIF Tower and nearby King Abdullah Financial District buildings damaged by the 19 Nov Houthi attack, Saudi Civil Defence reports no injuries; Houthis claim they 'targeted King Khalid International Airport and the Financial Center in Riyadh' (ToI 22:23); coalition destroys a ballistic missile and two drones heading south early Fri 20 Nov, Abha/Khamis Mushait warnings issued and withdrawn; Saudi Arabia 'won't tolerate attacks on its land' and reserves 'all necessary measures'; UAE condemns; JMIC: further attacks on commercial vessels 'highly likely'
items.headline: US-Israel-Iran War: Key Updates for UAE Residents (Nov 20) / Times of Israel liveblog Nov 19 10:23 pm
items.claim: Gulf News (20 Nov 09:06 UAE): a Houthi attack damaged the PIF Tower, Saudi Arabia's tallest building, and nearby buildings in the King Abdullah Financial District; Saudi Civil Defence reported no injuries; earlier the coalition intercepted missiles aimed at Riyadh and the south; early Friday it destroyed a ballistic missile and two drones heading south; Civil Defence issued then withdrew warnings in Abha and Khamis Mushait; Saudi Arabia warned it won't tolerate attacks on its land and reserved the right to take 'all necessary measures'; the UAE condemned the attacks as a violation of Saudi sovereignty; the Joint Maritime Information Center warned further attacks on commercial vessels are 'highly likely'. Times of Israel liveblog (19 Nov 10:23pm): Houthis say they 'targeted King Khalid International Airport and the Financial Center in Riyadh', no immediate Saudi confirmation; (06:07am) coalition 'dealt with a missile threat launched by Yemen's Houthis towards Riyadh', Saudi airstrikes on Sanaa early Thursday.
items.source: Gulf News 20 Nov 09:06 UAE; Times of Israel liveblog 19 Nov 06:07am, 08:46am, 10:23pm; DTN 19 Nov (Houthi launches toward Riyadh as a price driver)
items.note: Update vs 11-19 on the Riyadh tower: no injuries, Houthi claim of responsibility naming the airport and financial centre as targets, and a Saudi 'all necessary measures' line - the Houthi front remains the main kinetic driver while no Iranian strike on Gulf states and no US strike on Iran surfaced in gate. The JMIC 'highly likely' advisory is the only maritime-regime statement in gate (no new CENTCOM/NAVCENT advisory after the 18 Nov STS rule). Saudi Joint Forces commander change (17 Nov, wajeehlion) is pre-gate.

items.name: Oil structure: Brent settles flat at 91.98 after a $2 swing (peak 93.50) with WTI Dec 83.21 at a 12-week low ahead of expiry; first Brent M2 print in six runs - Feb 89.44, Jan/Feb backwardation 2.54 (vs 2.57 on 15 Oct); Brent-WTI narrows to 8.77; Rabobank 'not yet at the point where the narrative of improving supply is enough to overshadow the military flare-ups'; Saxo 'liquidity is poor'; US energy chief: Hormuz flows at a record; Rabobank: flows 'have improved' but ships still attacked; European diesel at three-month low; Brent -20% in November, third weekly loss pending; OPEC+ 29 Nov
items.headline: Oil Prices Swing on Middle East Uncertainty / WTI Stuck Beneath $85 as Glut Fears Offset Supply Risks / Brent Crude Price $92.22: Third Weekly Drop Before OPEC+
items.claim: Bloomberg via Rigzone (19 Nov 5:31pm EST): Brent Jan settled 91.98 (+0.03%) after a ~$2 range, WTI Dec 83.21 (-0.06%, expires Friday), WTI Jan 82.44 (+0.2%); Brent down roughly 20% for the month; Schmit (Rabobank): 'We are not yet at the point where the narrative of improving supply is enough to overshadow the military flare-ups'; Hansen (Saxo): 'Liquidity is poor across the markets, which is understandable after a big drop'; the US energy chief said flows through Hormuz reached a record, Rabobank said flows 'have improved' but ships are still being attacked; IEA: the war could reshape energy markets for years and a quick resolution could make oil and gas buyers' markets; China Q4 import forecasts 9.8-10.2 mb/d (Energy Aspects, FGE, Rystad); European diesel futures at a three-month low. DTN (19 Nov 2:43pm CST): Brent Jan 91.98 (+0.03), Brent Feb 89.44 (+0.27), WTI Dec 83.21 (-0.05, high 84.88), WTI Jan 82.44 (+0.13), ULSD 3.9514, RBOB 2.4951, DXY 103.830; drivers - EIA builds, trilateral refined-product pledge, Putin abandoning any energy-infrastructure moratorium, Russian refinery runs down ~45% since late October, White House briefed on attack options, third carrier, three-tanker mine report, Houthi launches. financefeeds (20 Nov 07:00 GMT): Brent 92.22 at 01:18 GMT, on course for ~-3.5% on the week, third straight weekly decline; OPEC+ ministerial 29 Nov sets the 2027 framework; Reuters: Gulf crude shipments recovered 'towards pre-war levels'. cappnotes: energy sector -0.65%, smallest decline of 11 sectors on a day the Dow fell 2.2%.
items.source: Bloomberg via Rigzone 19 Nov 5:31pm EST; DTN 19 Nov 2:43pm CST; Reuters via financefeeds 20 Nov 07:00 GMT; cappnotes 19 Nov
items.note: O-panel: the market absorbed the Netanyahu campaign report, the Channel 12 'backed out' story, the IRGC 'definitive conclusion' line and the Axios deferral in a flat close - risk premium is being traded intraday ($2 range) and faded by the settle. The Brent M2 print restores a prompt-spread reading: 2.54 backwardation is unchanged from mid-October despite a $11 fall in flat price, i.e. the curve has shifted down roughly in parallel rather than flattening - the physical tightness signal persists while the level discounts surplus. The 'record flows' claim from the US energy chief versus hormuz.now 7%/tankers 3% and PortWatch 0.8% tonnage remains a methods conflict (escorted convoys and AIS-dark hulls), flagged not reconciled. Energy equities outperformed in a -2% tape.
